## A second, opposite symptom of the same root — measured today, offered as a second data point for this card

This card states the corollary that a local `merge-tree` of an os-regen path is not GitHub mergeability. Two independent instances turned up in the `domain:services` lane today, and they fail in **opposite directions** from the same cause. Recording both because a reader who has only met one will not recognise the other.

### Instance 1 — GitHub refuses a merge that is locally clean (PR #15838)

`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <head>` exited **0 with no conflict markers**, printing only the repo's own note that `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` is generated. GitHub reported **`mergeable_state: dirty`** and auto-merge never fired; the PR sat for an hour reading as "queued". ⇒ **The local probe said nothing to do, on a PR that would never merge.** Blobs at merge-base / `origin/main` / head were all three different, so both sides had touched it.

⚠️ The trap is that this is the *quietest possible* failure: a green probe plus an armed auto-merge looks exactly like a healthy wait.

### Instance 2 — git merges cleanly and produces a **semantically stale** file (PR #15966)

Same file, different outcome. `git merge origin/main` **succeeded**, text-merging the generated page with no conflict. The result was wrong:

- `check:system-context-census` is **green at `origin/main`** (`904e70780`, measured directly);
- it was **green on the branch** before the merge;
- it is **red on the merge product, with 26 problems** — and **every one is an anchor into `plugin-security` or `rest`**, files that branch never touches.

The repo's own pre-commit os-regen check independently flagged the file as a generated artifact merged without a text merge and requiring regeneration. Repaired with the census's `--fix`, after which it reports **105 elevation read sites across 44 files and 140 resolving anchors — identical to what `origin/main` reports**, so the repair restores the upstream reading rather than inventing one.

### Why the pair is worth more than either

⭐ **Both come from the same root — a generated file whose content is line anchors, being text-merged — and they present as opposites:** one refuses to merge while looking mergeable; the other merges while looking correct. A rule phrased only as *"a clean `merge-tree` is not GitHub mergeability"* covers the first and would let the second through, because in the second case GitHub is perfectly happy and so is git. ⇒ The reading that covers both is closer to: **for a `merge=os-regen` path, no merge result is trustworthy until the generator has re-run on the merge product.**

⚠️ And the second is the more dangerous of the two, because it is **silent**: the first stalls a PR visibly, while the second lands a wrong generated file unless a gate happens to read it. Here one did. There is no reason to assume that is general.

### One more property, from a third encounter today (PR #15838's resolution)

When the census's `--fix` was asked to repair that same page after an upstream row was added, it **refused**: *"the page anchors 9 distinct line(s) into this file, but the tree holds 8 anchorable line(s). The POPULATION changed, this is not a shift."* ⭐ That refusal is the behaviour that kept a hand-resolution from becoming silent anchor rot — the fix required a structural decision (two rows citing one site) before any number could be regenerated. Worth keeping in view for whatever probe this card lands on: **a generator that refuses when the population changed is doing more for correctness than one that always succeeds.**

⛔ Filed as data, not as a proposed remedy — the sound-probe question is this card's and it is the maintainer's to settle.

The line ratchet on `AGENTS.md` rises from 1162 to **1171** for this PR's ten-line corollary (local `merge-tree` is not GitHub mergeability; probe from a driver-less bare clone; ⛔ never `-c merge.os-regen.driver=`). Re-wrap and cross-file moves were correctly refused; this is the header's escape hatch — a maintainer ruling quoted in the PR body. Patch round: the ceiling line in the ratchet map, one `ruledRaises` record quoting this comment, PR body citing it; then the maintainer merges by hand (governed surface).

Sequencing ruled: this PR lands first; #15856 (the rules-only rewrite, re-pinning to 1058) rebases onto it and re-typesets this bullet in its own voice, with its ask becoming 1058 → 1068 or whatever its trimmed count measures.

## Correction to the ceiling ruling, and the director seat now drives this PR to merge (2026-09-07)

Maintainer reply, verbatim: 「15885 你接手跟进合并」.

**Correction.** The batch #63 ruling above said "this PR lands first; #15856 rebases onto it". That sequencing was already false when written: #15856 (the rules-only rewrite) merged on 2026-09-05T13:48Z as `abdceef8c`, and `AGENTS.md` on `main` is now **1058** lines with the ratchet ceiling re-pinned to 1058. So the ruled number 1171 no longer describes anything. The ruling's substance stands — the ten-line corollary is approved and its raise is the header's escape hatch — and the number is re-measured mechanically: a driver-less text merge of this branch onto `main` is clean and lands `AGENTS.md` at **1068** (merge tree `ad22eca70`, the bullet at §11 lines 586–595, directly under the "LOCAL facility" sentence it anchors to).

**Patch round (director seat, via a dev seat in a worktree; governed posture unchanged):**
1. Merge `origin/main` into `claude/issue-15871-agents-merge-tree-corollary` (no rebase, no force-push).
2. Re-typeset the bullet in #15856's rules-only voice — the incident clause "and it has already cost a seat a round trip" comes out; every rule sentence (the corollary, the mechanism, the driver-less probe with both commands, the ⛔ `-c merge.os-regen.driver=` refusal and its reason) stays; ≤120 bytes per line.
3. Raise `CEILINGS` for `AGENTS.md` in `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` from 1058 to the **measured landed count** (1068 or fewer), headroom 0, with the entry comment quoting this ruling verbatim: batch #63 「同意」 and today's 「15885 你接手跟进合并」. `AGENTS.md` is not a `CROSS_FILE_MOVES` destination, so no `ruledRaises` record applies (the batch #63 text's mention of one is withdrawn).
4. PR body cites this comment; gates re-run at the new head; push.

The maintainer's approval and armed auto-merge stand; if the push dismisses the approval, the maintainer will be asked to re-approve once, with the gate readings in hand.

So no re-approval is needed on account of this push. Auto-merge was left exactly as armed; no seat flipped ready, enqueued, or approved.

I did **not** re-PATCH to re-add it: durable attribution is already in the body prose and the standing rule forbids looping on the footer. Flagging rather than fixing.
2. **The `needs-user-decision` label is now stale** — the ruling it was waiting on has landed and is quoted in the body. Removing it is the director's/PM's call, not mine, so it is untouched.

## Patch round landed — head `f0e9c4c87`; one red remains and it is the by-design kind #16502 ruled on (director seat, 2026-09-07 08:4x UTC)

**What landed** (dev seat, worktree, plain push): merge of `main` (`f171510dc`, clean, the tree the correction comment measured), the corollary re-typeset rules-only at §11 (10 lines in, 10 out, ≤ 90 bytes/line), `CEILINGS['AGENTS.md']` 1058 → **1068** with both rulings quoted verbatim in the entry comment, no `ruledRaises` (AGENTS.md is not a `CROSS_FILE_MOVES` destination — read, not assumed). 36 gate families derived and run, all exit 0: `check:pm-skill-ratchet` — *AGENTS.md is 1068 lines (ceiling 1068; headroom 0)*; ratchet self-test 157/157; `check:pm-dispatch-gates` 1534 cases. Ablation: ceiling back to 1058 ⇒ red with the 1058-vs-1068 message; restore proven by blob hash. Approval survival measured through the repo's own `authorizedApprovalVerdict` on `f0e9c4c87`: **approved, os-zhuang** — no re-approval needed. Auto-merge (armed by the maintainer 2026-09-05) is untouched. Stale `needs-user-decision` label removed.

**The one red: `Part-of PR must not also close its card`.** Standing-down note per the #16502 ruling (C), not a fix request:
- It fires on the branch's **original** commit `ca2088e3d` (2026-09-05), whose message carries `Part of #15815`. That commit predates the rule; the gate reached this PR through the merge of `main`, which is why it was green on the previous head and red now.
- It is unclearable by any permitted act: the gate reads every commit on the PR, so a new commit cannot remove it, and rewriting pushed history is forbidden (`AGENTS.md`, three sites). Its own header names the remedy as the squash message being taken from the PR body at merge.
- It is not a required context and does not run on `merge_group` (#16502's measurements), so the maintainer's armed auto-merge proceeds once the required checks are green. Residual risk: the `Part of #15815` line lands in the squash message under today's `COMMIT_MESSAGES` setting — it closes nothing (`Fixes #15871` is in the body only). ⚠️ The setting change D (`squash_merge_commit_message` → `PR_BODY`), ruled on #16502, is still pending on the maintainer's side (read at 08:4x: `COMMIT_MESSAGES`); #16516 carries the rule text that names this third case.

Nothing further is owed by this PR. The remaining checks are in progress at the time of writing; auto-merge takes it from there.
